changelog: [When to Segment]: Narrowed the noun-phrase+particle permissive rule so it only licenses a boundary when the eventual predicate is a plain matrix verb — explicitly excluding cases where the pending predicate is a reporting/opinion verb (-다고, -것 같다), a governing verb that assigns role/meaning to the phrase, or a postposed subject/topic marker not yet seen. Also excluded mid-repetition of an idiomatic/connective phrase whose sense is only fixed by the following clause, cross-referencing the new [Never Segment] rule. This targets the four placement failures where a boundary was cut before the element that determines the clause's true meaning had arrived.

[Never Segment]: Added one general rule prohibiting a boundary at the end of a clause that is grammatically dependent on a later reporting/opinion verb, an unarrived governing verb, an unarrived postposed subject/topic marker, or a repeated/idiomatic phrase disambiguated only by its following clause — these are wrong at any budget because the emitted piece asserts something the rest of the sentence later contradicts.
